summary: LLM inference costs scale directly with token consumption, and unoptimized production systems routinely overspend by 50-80% on redundant API calls, bloated prompts, and oversized models. By combining prompt caching, semantic caching, model cascading, and prompt compression, teams can cut inference spend from roughly $10K to $2K monthly (an 80% reduction) while often improving latency. Most of these techniques require modest engineering effort and preserve output quality.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching (KV cache reuse)
techniques.description: Reuses precomputed key-value tensors for repeated prompt prefixes (system prompts, few-shot examples, long documents) so identical leading tokens are not reprocessed on each call. Providers apply a steep discount to cached input tokens.
techniques.savings: Up to 90% reduction on input token cost for repeated prefixes
techniques.example: Place your large static system prompt and document context at the beginning of every request so Anthropic/OpenAI automatically caches the shared prefix, charging full price only for the changing user query.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Caches LLM responses keyed by the embedding (semantic meaning) of the query rather than exact string match, so paraphrased or similar questions return a stored answer without a new model call.
techniques.savings: 60-70% reduction (reported ~68% cache hit rates in production)
techniques.example: Use GPTCache or a Redis semantic cache to embed incoming queries; if cosine similarity to a cached query exceeds 0.95, return the cached response instead of calling the API.

techniques.name: Model Cascading / Routing
techniques.description: Routes simple queries to cheaper/smaller models and escalates only hard queries to larger, more expensive models, often using a confidence check or a lightweight classifier as the router.
techniques.example: Send all requests first to GPT-4o-mini or Claude Haiku, and only escalate to GPT-4o or Claude Sonnet when the small model's confidence or a validator flags the answer as insufficient.

techniques.name: Prompt Optimization / Compression
techniques.description: Trims verbose instructions, removes redundant few-shot examples, and compresses context (e.g., with LLMLingua) to reduce input tokens while preserving task performance.
techniques.example: Replace a 500-token multi-paragraph instruction with a concise 150-token version and use LLMLingua to compress retrieved RAG context before sending it to the model.

techniques.name: Output Token Limiting & Structured Output
techniques.description: Caps max_tokens, requests concise or structured (JSON/enum) responses, and avoids open-ended generation to reduce expensive output tokens, which are often billed 2-5x higher than input.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=150 and prompt 'Answer with a single JSON object, no explanation' so the model returns only the fields you need.

techniques.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) context pruning
techniques.description: Instead of stuffing entire documents into the prompt, retrieve and inject only the top-k most relevant chunks, drastically cutting input tokens on knowledge-heavy tasks.
techniques.savings: 40-70% reduction in input tokens for document-based tasks
techniques.example: Rank retrieved chunks by relevance and pass only the top 3 (instead of 20) to the model, optionally reranking with a cross-encoder to keep quality high.

techniques.name: Request Batching & Async Processing
techniques.description: Groups multiple requests into a single batched/async call or uses provider batch APIs that offer discounted off-peak pricing for non-latency-sensitive workloads.
techniques.savings: Up to 50% reduction via batch API discounts
techniques.example: Submit overnight bulk summarization jobs through OpenAI's Batch API to get a ~50% discount versus real-time calls.

techniques.name: Fine-tuned / Smaller Specialized Models
techniques.description: Replace a large general model with a smaller model (or distilled/fine-tuned one) for narrow, high-volume tasks where it matches quality at a fraction of the per-token cost.
techniques.savings: 60-90% reduction on per-token cost for targeted tasks
techniques.example: Swap GPT-4o for a fine-tuned GPT-4o-mini on your classification task once it reaches equivalent accuracy on your eval set.

techniques.name: Streaming & Early Termination
techniques.description: Stream responses and stop generation as soon as the required content (e.g., a parsed answer or stop sequence) is produced to avoid paying for unneeded trailing tokens.
techniques.example: Define a stop sequence like '</answer>' so generation halts immediately after the answer rather than continuing into filler.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching library for LLMs that stores and retrieves responses by embedding similarity to cut redundant API calls.

tools.name: Redis / Redis Semantic Cache
tools.description: Vector-enabled Redis used as a high-performance semantic cache storing query embeddings and responses for sub-millisecond cache hits.
tools.pricing_paid: Redis Cloud paid tiers from ~$5/mo; Redis OSS free

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK for 100+ LLM providers with built-in caching, routing, model fallbacks, and cost tracking under one OpenAI-compatible API.
tools.pricing_paid: Open source free; LiteLLM Enterprise custom pricing

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform providing request logging, cost analytics, caching, and prompt management via a proxy.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (10k requests/mo); paid plans from ~$20/mo

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: Framework for building LLM apps with built-in caching layers (in-memory, Redis, SQLite), prompt templating, and RAG orchestration.
tools.pricing_paid: Open source free; LangSmith paid plans from ~$39/user/mo

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft prompt-compression tool that reduces prompt token count up to 20x using a small language model while retaining task performance.

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway offering semantic caching, load balancing, routing, fallbacks, and observability across multiple LLM providers.

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.description: Unified API router that gives access to many models with transparent per-token pricing and automatic cheapest-provider routing.
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-as-you-go per token; small routing fee on credits

quick_wins: Enable provider prompt caching by keeping static system prompts and context at the start of every request to get up to 90% off repeated input tokens.
Add a semantic cache (GPTCache or Redis) in front of your API to deflect 60-70% of repeated/similar queries.
Set a sensible max_tokens and request concise/structured output to stop paying for unneeded, expensive output tokens.
Route easy requests to a cheap small model (GPT-4o-mini / Claude Haiku) and only escalate hard ones to a flagship model.
Trim and compress prompts: remove redundant instructions and prune RAG context to the top few most relevant chunks.
